data.name: Raktim
data.gender_notes: Raktim is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who has a red color. The name Raktim carries the meaning “Red” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Bengali. Parents who choose Raktim usually hope their child will grow to embody red and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the power of love and passion.
data.etymology: Raktim belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Red.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Raktim total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Rama is considered to be the ideal king, a paragon of virtue, wisdom, and justice, whose story is portrayed in the epic Ramayana.
data.spiritual_significance: Rama represents the divine, pure, and selfless embodiment of dharma or righteousness and aided in the protecting of moral values and upholding the harmony in society.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Raktim, derived from the Sanskrit word 'rakta' meaning 'blood,' symbolizes the embodiment of life force and vitality. It represents the passion, courage, and strength within an individual, reminding us of the power of our inner spirit.

historical_references.reference: According to Indian mythology, Raktim was a name of Lord Shiva during the 'Tandava' dance performance. During this dance, Lord Shiva's body was covered in a furious rage and his body turned red, symbolizing the 'Rudra' form of Shiva. This dance is said to have caused the creation and destruction of the universe.

Raktim Chetia, a famous Assamese king of the Koch dynasty (15th-17th centuries), ruled over parts of Assam and Bengal. He is remembered for his military prowess and expansion of his kingdom, which included establishing the city of Jalpaiguri and the temple of Triveni Mata.
